duga-tagline: The project tagline, shown under the name on the home page. Keep it short. In your language, feel free to choose a natural local term rather than transliterating "queer" if there's a better-established one -- see the /about page for the terminology policy.
duga-nav-home: Link label in the site navigation, goes back to the home page.
duga-nav-about: Link label in the site navigation, goes to the About page.
duga-home-title: The project name, shown as the main heading on the home page. This is a proper noun ("Duga") -- most languages should leave it untranslated, like a brand name.
duga-home-intro: One-paragraph explanation of what Duga is, shown on the home page below the title.
duga-home-pick-language: Label above the list of languages a visitor can choose to browse.
duga-home-interface-language: Label for the interface-language switcher: a dropdown of languages used to translate the site's own UI, independent of which language's content a visitor is browsing.
duga-home-interface-language-submit: Button label to submit the interface-language switcher form.
duga-lang-home-title: Page heading for a single language's overview. $1 is the autonym of that language (e.g. "Français").
duga-lang-home-placeholder: Placeholder shown on a language overview page before gap detection exists yet (milestone M0/M1). Will be replaced with real content in a later milestone.
duga-lang-home-back: Link back to the home page's language list.
duga-about-title: Page heading for the About page.
duga-about-name: Explains the meaning of the project name "Duga" on the About page. Keep "Duga" itself untranslated.
duga-about-body: One-paragraph restatement of the project's purpose, shown on the About page.
duga-about-license: States the software license on the About page.
duga-footer-status: Shown in the page footer while the project has no real data yet. Will be removed once detectors ship.
duga-404-title: Heading shown on the not-found error page.
duga-404-body: Body text on the not-found error page, explaining a link may point to a language that isn't set up yet.
